title: Golden Hour: Sunset Forecast
shortDescription: Which evenings are worth it, and a plan for the ones that are.
fullDescription:
Which evenings are worth it, and a plan for the ones that are.

Golden Hour rates every coming sunset from 0.0 to 5.0 for the places you care about. Open it and the top of the screen says Go tonight, Maybe tonight or Not tonight, why, and one time: sunset, and when to be there. On a Not tonight, it names the next good evening.

Where to watch: landmarks, adventurous spots, dining with a view and your own places, from OpenStreetMap. Each one says how far away it is, how easy it is to reach, and whether the map lists parking and toilets nearby. Filter by Parking, Toilets and Short walk.

A plan in one tap: when to leave, when to be there, sunset, when the afterglow ends, and when to start back so the walk is done before dark. Set your own arrive-by, travel time and home-by, add a note, and tick off what to bring.

Getting home: every plan says when to start back, and offers “Text a friend where I’ll be” and “I’m home”. Golden Hour never claims a place is lit or safe.

Share a picture of tonight, the week or a plan, with a link anyone can open. Changed the plan? Send update says what changed. Add to calendar fills in a new event in your calendar app.

The evenings ahead: the next few evenings rated, and exact sunset times for any date up to a year away, with golden hour and blue hour.

The sky behind each place is its own sunset forecast. Imperial and metric side by side.

When the forecast can’t be reached, it says so and keeps the last one, marked with how old it is.

Your places, plans and sunset log stay on your phone and never reach me. To get forecasts and places, Golden Hour sends the coordinates of your places to Open-Meteo, to OpenStreetMap’s Overpass servers and to OpenFreeMap for the map; a venue search sends what you type to Photon. The app’s pages come from GitHub Pages. Location is optional: “Use my location” asks for your approximate location only when you tap it.

A forecast is not a promise. Times are estimates, so keep an eye on the sky and on the way home.

Free and open source (MIT License). No ads, no account, no tracking.
